exposure: CADASIL (Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy)
Cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL)
finding: CADASIL does not appear to be associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes for mothers or babies, with no increased risk of stroke during pregnancy or negative effects on fetal growth observed.
mod_finding: This study found no evidence to suggest that CADASIL leads to an unfavorable pregnancy outcome for women or fetuses or that it necessitates preventative antithrombotic treatment during pregnancy.
birth_weight: In line with the general population (for the 6 prospectively followed patients)
